sounds.intro: Latvian uses the Latin alphabet with extra marks: macrons (ā, ē, ī, ū) for long vowels, and cedillas and carons for special consonants. It is a Baltic language, related to Lithuanian but not to Russian. Stress is almost always on the first syllable.
rows: soft "l" and soft "n", like "ly" in "million" and "ny" in "canyon"
notes: Latvian has six cases and no articles. Stress is on the first syllable of every word, which makes it easy to read.
The pool is unreviewed. Some rarer words are best guesses.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Latvian has "tu" (you, informal) and "jūs" (you, formal or plural). Verb forms change for each person. There is no he / she difference in the plural except for gender in the past: "viņi" (they, men) and "viņas" (they, women).

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Latvian has no "the" or "a". Nouns end in -s, -š, -is, -us (masculine) or -a, -e (feminine). Plural masculine: -i (grāmata, grāmatas). Memorise the plural of each noun.

grammar.title: To be: būt
text: The verb "būt" (to be) changes for each person, and is also used for "there is".

grammar.title: Having: man ir
text: Latvian says "to me is": man ir mašīna (I have a car). The thing owned comes after "ir". For "I do not have", use "man nav".

grammar.title: Present tense
text: Verbs change for person. Regular verbs (like "lasīt", to read) take -u, -i, -a for I, you, he / she: es lasu, tu lasi, viņš lasa.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The usual order is subject, verb, object: "es lasu grāmatu" (I read a book). The object ends change (a "case" ending): grāmata becomes grāmatu.

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put "ne" before the verb: es nezinu (I do not know). Verbs become "ne" + verb. With "būt", "nav" replaces "ir": man nav (I do not have). Nouns after "nav" take the genitive.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add "vai" at the start to turn a sentence into a yes / no question: Vai tu esi students? (Are you a student?). Answer "jā" (yes) or "nē" (no).

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words come at the start of the sentence.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Latvian possessives change with the gender and number of the noun: mans (m), mana (f), mani (m pl), manas (f pl). Your: tavs, tava. His, her: viņa, viņas (no change). "Patikt" means "to please": man patīk tēja (tea pleases me).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: Use "jūs" (and "jūs esat") for one older person, a stranger or in a formal setting. Use "tu" with friends, family and children.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: past forms of verbs (es lasīju, I read). Future: end in -šu (es lasīšu, I will read). A form changes by gender in the past of "būt": es biju, tu biji, viņš bija.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Use the "tu" form: ej! (go!), nāc! (come!). Add "-iet" for "jūs": ejiet! For "do not", use "neej!" or "nenāc!".

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: "Varēt" (can), "vajadzēt" or "drīkstēt" (must / may) and "gribēt" (want) change for person. They are followed by the "to" form of the verb: es varu peldēt (I can swim).
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Prepositions: "uz" (on, to), "zem" (under), "blakus" (next to), "pie" (at, by), "tuvu" (near), "iekšā" or "ar locative" (in): mājās (at home), skolā (at school). Nouns after a preposition change case.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add "-āks" to an adjective for "more": liels, lielāks (big, bigger). For "the most", use "visvairāk" or "vislielākais". "Nekā" means "than".
